item.title: Some current, former Columbia City Council members unhappy with swift vote on Flock contract
item.description:
The City of Columbia's contract with Flock will not renew after its expiration in March 2027.

Following a nearly four-hour special hearing at City Hall Tuesday night, with more than 50 residents stepping up to speak, Ward 2 Councilwoman Vera Elwood moved to vote on the automated license plate readers.

The motion passed 5-2, with Ward 3 Councilwoman Jacque Sample and Ward 6 Councilwoman Betsy Peters making up the “no” votes.

Sample took to Facebook after the meeting, claiming the call for a vote took her by surprise.

item.title: NT Daily 11/10: Rural Health Care Funding, Downtown Investment & Mizzou Basketball History | Jefferson City News-Tribune
item.description:
On today's NT Daily, Erin Schrimpf kicks off a new Thanksgiving recipe tradition and previews Thursday's Holiday Mart JC. Plus, Gov. Mike Kehoe announces more than $55 million in rural health care funding, raising questions about Medicaid and the future of rural hospitals.
Downtown Jefferson City receives federal Opportunity Zone approval, creating new opportunities for investment and development.
We also look at Little Explorers' upcoming Princess Party and an $11 million adventure park planned by the owners of Stark Caverns.
In sports, Mizzou freshman Jason Crowe Jr. makes history with a record-breaking 34-point performance against SIU-Edwardsville.
This episode is brought to you by MU Health Care, Hen House and Coleman Appliance.
Read more at NewsTribune.com.
